rationale: B is better because it organizes the design space by compression granularity, clearly distinguishes coverage loss from precision loss, and gives the stronger workload-specific recommendation: whole-repository coding has sparse, delayed relevance, so preserving token coverage through GQA and KV quantization—and using retrieval before attention—is safer than irreversible attention-based pruning. A identifies the same risk but then recommends SnapKV compression based on a short prompt-tail observation window, which conflicts with its own premise that relevant code can be unpredictable and anywhere in the repository; its final memory arithmetic also conflates quantized bytes with effective retained tokens. B contains technical inaccuracies—notably its PyramidKV layer-budget description appears reversed, and its descriptions of Scissorhands, Quest, FastGen, and CacheGen are oversimplified or partly misleading—but its central comparison, quality-risk analysis, and recommendation remain more sound and actionable.
